translations.literal: Because the grass in the royal camp was overgrown and foul, Sheng wished to have Tuli personally remove it himself to show the tribes and make clear imperial authority; he therefore pointed to the grass before the tent and said, "This root is very fragrant."
translations.idiomatic: Because the grass in the royal camp was overgrown, Sheng wished Tuli to clear it himself to display imperial authority to the tribes; he pointed to the grass before the tent and said, "This root is very fragrant."

sentences.zh: 」染幹遽嗅之曰：「殊不香也。

translations.literal: " Tuli hastily sniffed it and said, "It is not fragrant at all."
translations.idiomatic: " Tuli hastily sniffed it and said, "It is not fragrant at all."

sentences.zh: 」晟曰：「天子行幸所在，諸侯躬親灑掃，耘除禦路，以表至敬之心。

translations.literal: " Sheng said, "Wherever the Son of Heaven travels on tour, the feudal lords personally sprinkle and sweep, hoe and clear the imperial road, to express the utmost reverent heart."
translations.idiomatic: " Sheng said, "Wherever the Son of Heaven travels, the feudal lords personally sweep and clear the imperial road to show their utmost reverence."

sentences.zh: 今牙中蕪穢，謂是留香草耳。

translations.literal: Now the camp is overgrown and foul—you must think this is fragrant grass left in place."
translations.idiomatic: Now the camp is overgrown—you must think this is fragrant grass left for the emperor."

sentences.zh: 」染幹乃悟曰：「奴罪過。

translations.literal: " Tuli then understood and said, "Your slave has sinned."
translations.idiomatic: " Tuli then understood and said, "Your slave has sinned."

sentences.zh: 奴之骨肉，皆天子賜也，得效筋力，豈敢有辭？

translations.literal: Your slave's flesh and bone were all bestowed by the Son of Heaven; to be able to exert muscle and strength—how would I dare refuse?
translations.idiomatic: Your slave's very flesh and bone were bestowed by the Son of Heaven; how dare I refuse to exert my strength?

sentences.zh: 特以邊人不知法耳，賴將軍恩澤而教導之。

translations.literal: It is only that the frontier people do not know the law; I rely upon the general's grace and favor to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: It is only that we frontier people do not know the law; I rely on the general's grace to instruct us.

sentences.zh: 將軍之惠，奴之幸也。

translations.literal: The general's kindness is your slave's good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The general's kindness is your slave's good fortune.

sentences.zh: 」遂拔所佩刀，親自芟草，其貴人及諸部爭放效之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon drew the knife at his belt and personally cut the grass; his nobles and the various tribes vied to imitate him.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew the knife at his belt and personally cut the grass; his nobles and the tribes all vied to follow his example.

sentences.zh: 乃發榆林北境，至於其牙，又東達於薊，長三千里，廣百步，舉國就役而開禦道。

translations.literal: They then set out from the northern border of Yulin as far as the royal camp, and eastward as far as Ji—three thousand li in length and a hundred paces in width—the whole state taking labor to open the imperial road.
translations.idiomatic: They then opened a road from the northern border of Yulin to the royal camp and eastward to Ji—three thousand li long and a hundred paces wide—with the whole nation mobilized to build the imperial highway.

sentences.zh: 帝聞晟策，乃益嘉焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of Sheng's stratagem, he praised him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of Sheng's stratagem, he praised him all the more.

sentences.zh: 後除淮陽太守，未赴任，複為右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was made Administrator of Huaiyang but did not take up the post; he was again appointed General of the Right Agile Cavalry Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made administrator of Huaiyang but did not take up the post and was again appointed general of the Right Agile Cavalry Guards.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，時年五十八。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, at the age of fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he died, at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 帝深悼惜之，賵贈甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply mourned and regretted him, and the funeral gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned him and gave lavish funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 後突厥圍雁門，帝歎曰：「向使長孫晟在，不令匈奴至此！

translations.literal: Later, when the Türks besieged Yanmen, the emperor sighed and said, "If only Zhangsun Sheng were still alive, he would not have let the Xiongnu reach this point!"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Türks besieged Yanmen, the emperor sighed and said, "If Zhangsun Sheng were still alive, the Xiongnu would never have reached this far!"

sentences.zh: 」晟好奇計，務功名。

translations.literal: " Sheng delighted in unusual stratagems and pursued fame and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: " Sheng delighted in unusual stratagems and pursued fame and achievement.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，居憂毀瘠，為朝士所稱。

translations.literal: By nature he was supremely filial; in mourning he wasted away, and was praised by the court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was supremely filial; in mourning he wasted away, and the court praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，追贈司空、上柱國、齊國公，諡曰獻。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he was posthumously granted Minister of Works, Senior Pillar of State, and Duke of the State of Qi; his posthumous title was Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era he was posthumously made Minister of Works, Senior Pillar of State, and Duke of Qi; his posthumous title was Xian.

sentences.zh: 少子無忌嗣。

translations.literal: His youngest son Wuji succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Wuji succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 其長子行布，亦多謀略，有父風。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xingbu also had many stratagems and bore his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xingbu was also resourceful and bore his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 起家漢王諒庫真，甚見親狎。

translations.literal: He first entered service as a kuzhen attendant to Prince Liang of Han and was greatly favored and intimate.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a kuzhen attendant to Prince Liang of Han and was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 後遇諒於并州起逆，率眾南拒官軍，乃留行布城守，遂與豆盧毓等閉門拒諒，城陷，遇害。

translations.literal: Later, when Liang rebelled at Bingzhou and led his followers south to resist the imperial army, he left Xingbu to hold the city in defense; Xingbu then closed the gates with Dou Luyu and others to resist Liang, but when the city fell he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang rebelled at Bingzhou and marched south against the imperial army, he left Xingbu to defend the city; Xingbu closed the gates with Dou Luyu and others to resist Liang, but when the city fell he was killed.

sentences.zh: 次子恆安，以兄功授鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: The second son Heng'an, on account of his elder brother's merit, was appointed Commandant of the Hawkish Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Heng'an was appointed commandant of the Hawkish Guards on account of his elder brother's merit.

sentences.zh: 史評史臣曰：長孫氏爰自代陰，來儀京洛，門傳鍾鼎，家誓山河。

translations.literal: The historian's appraisal: The historiographer says, "The Zhangsun clan from of old in Dai and Yin came to settle at the capital Luoyang; their house transmitted bell and tripod, and their family pledged itself to the mountains and rivers."
translations.idiomatic: The historian's appraisal: The historiographer writes, "The Zhangsun clan, from Dai and Yin of old, came to settle at Luoyang; their house bore the emblems of nobility and pledged itself to the realm."

sentences.zh: 漢代八王，無以方其茂績；

translations.literal: The eight kings of Han cannot be matched against their abundant achievements;
translations.idiomatic: The eight kings of Han cannot match their abundant achievements;

sentences.zh: 張氏七葉，不能譬此重光。

translations.literal: the seven generations of the Zhang clan cannot be compared with this repeated glory.
translations.idiomatic: nor can the seven generations of the Zhang clan compare with this repeated glory.

sentences.zh: 覽獨擅雄辨，熾早稱爽俊，俱司禮閣，並統師旅，且公且侯，文武不墜。

translations.literal: Lan alone excelled in forceful eloquence; Chi was early acclaimed as bright and outstanding; both served the ritual offices and both commanded armies and hosts—dukes and marquises together, civil and martial never fallen away.
translations.idiomatic: Lan excelled in eloquence; Chi was early acclaimed as brilliant; both served the ritual offices and commanded armies—dukes and marquises together, civil and martial achievement unbroken.

sentences.zh: 晟體資英武，兼包奇略，因機制變，懷彼戎夷。

translations.literal: Sheng's person was endowed with heroic martial prowess and embraced extraordinary stratagems; adapting to opportunity he controlled change and held the barbarians of the Rong and Yi in his grasp.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was endowed with heroic martial prowess and extraordinary stratagems; adapting to opportunity he controlled the barbarian peoples.

sentences.zh: 傾巢盡落，屈膝稽顙，塞垣絕鳴鏑之旅，渭橋有單于之拜。

translations.literal: Their nests were overturned and all fell; they bent the knee and knocked the forehead; along the frontier wall the journeys of whistling arrows ceased, and at Wei Bridge there was the khan's bow.
translations.idiomatic: Their power was overturned and all submitted; they bent the knee; along the frontier the whistling arrows ceased, and at Wei Bridge the khan performed his obeisance.

sentences.zh: 惠流邊朔，功光王府，保茲爵祿，不亦宜乎！

translations.literal: His kindness flowed to the northern frontier; his achievements illumined the royal house; to preserve such rank and emolument—is it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: His kindness flowed to the northern frontier and his achievements illumined the royal house; to preserve such rank and emolument was only fitting!
